title: SLO surge mitigation blueprint and compact runbooks
author: Aisha Chen
content:
Overview:

This page is a compact, decision-focused playbook for SLO surge events and other progressive degradations that commonly affect Redwood’s inference platform (latency spikes, KV cache thrash, burst rate-limits, model quality regressions, and database-backed control-plane slowdowns). It is intended for first responders, bridge operators, and customer-success liaisons who need a fast, repeatable path from detection to containment, stabilization, customer notice, and post-incident evidence capture.

Goals:
- Rapid containment: stop customer-visible impact within the first 15 minutes where possible.
- Clear decision points: one-page decision ladder to decide rollback, fallback, or capacity scale actions.
- Customer-first comms: staged templates for internal and external notices.
- Compact runbooks: short, executable runbooks (<= 25 steps) for common surge classes.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments where Redwood controls serving or routing.
- For air-gapped/private on-prem incidents, follow on-prem escalation in eng-private-deployments.
- For security incidents (data exfiltration, credentials compromise) use security-and-compliance incident processes instead.

Roles and responsibilities:
- First Responder (FR): initial triage, runbook execution, escalate within 10 minutes if no stabilization.
- Bridge Operator (BO): runs the incident bridge, owns status cadence and customer comms.
- SRE/Serving Runtime Pager (SV): executes capacity/scale/rollback controls.
- Model Quality Lead (MQL): assesses model regressions and approves model fallback.
- Customer Success Liaison (CSL): drafts customer notices, monitors impacted customers.

Signal matrix (short):
(ASCII table)
| Signal source | Typical trigger | Initial FR action | Threshold (escalate) |
|---------------|-----------------|-------------------|----------------------|
| Prometheus SLO alerts | p50/p95 latency breaches, error-rate > SLO | Acknowledge, capture recent traces, open bridge | sustained >5m or >3% user impact |
| Tracing/Flamegraphs | sudden tail latency on specific endpoints | Collect traces, identify hot functions/kernels | latency-correlated with specific model shard |
| Logs / KV evictions | Cache-miss rate > baseline * 10 | Check cache nodes, eviction logs, restart node if unhealthy | persistent >=10min & errors increase |
| API consumer telemetry | spike in retry traffic or 429s | Identify top callers, apply per-tenant throttles | retries causing 30% of traffic |

Decision ladder (one-page):
1) Confirm impact: Is customer traffic failing or timing out? If NO, continue monitoring with increased sampling. If YES, proceed.
2) Localize: Is the degradation localized to region/pool/model variant? If localized, isolate pool and route traffic away.
3) Severity-based action:
   - Severity P1 (global >20% customers impacted OR SLO down >30m): Initiate mitigation + urgent page to SRE and Eng oncall. Consider emergency capacity scale or global fallback.
   - Severity P2 (targeted customers or spike <20%): Apply tenant throttles, activate burst pool, or fall back to lower-cost/quantized model variant.
4) If quality regression (answers wrong, hallucinating): Quarantine model version, switch to previous known-good model variant, and notify MQL.
5) When stabilized: run a postmortem evidence capture checklist, and prepare customer-facing summary.

Compact runbooks (short, copyable):
A. Latency spike affecting p95 in eu-west-1
- Step 1: FR acknowledges Prom alert and opens bridge: #incident-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.
- Step 2: Check region overview dashboard (Console > Per-region SLOs): note p50/p95 trends.
- Step 3: Identify top 3 services/models by trace count in last 10 min via tracing UI.
- Step 4: If single-serving pool is saturated, run:
  - CLI: redwood infra pool scale --region eu-west-1 --pool inference-pool-42 --delta +4 --reason "p95 spike"
- Step 5: If pool scale unavailable or slow, update routing policy to spill to fallback pool:
  - API call: POST /routing/v1/policies/activate {"policy":"spill-fallback-eu"} (example)
- Step 6: If latency persists after 10m, apply temporary global N-quantization variant for heavy models:
  - Deploy command: redwood serving switch-model --service text-gen --from v2.1 --to v2.0-quant --mode emergency
- Step 7: Track customer impact and update bridge every 10 minutes.
- Step 8: When p95 returns < SLO for 15m, reverse emergency actions in reverse order and document timeline.

B. KV cache thrash / mass-evictions
- Step 1: Acknowledge alert and examine eviction logs (log path /var/log/kv-evict.log) and metrics cache.evictions/sec.
- Step 2: Identify whether candidate causes are garbage collection, OOMs, or topology change.
- Step 3: If OOM on node: cordon node and restart shard:
  - CLI: redwood nodes cordon --id node-123 && redwood nodes restart --id node-123 --reason "oom-eviction"
- Step 4: If global thrash, enable read-through fallback (serve from prefix cache snapshot) and enable sticky-routing to warm nodes.
- Step 5: If root cause is a recent rollout, roll back that deploy immediately with: redwood deploy rollback --service kv-cache --to tag/2026-05-21
- Step 6: Notify affected customers if eviction caused request failures > 1%.

C. Rate limit surge caused by noisy tenant
- Step 1: Identify top callers by telemetry: top 10 tokens/requests in last 5 minutes.
- Step 2: Apply per-tenant soft throttles: POST /quota/v1/tenants/<id>/throttle {"rate":200rps} with 5m TTL.
- Step 3: If client does not back off, escalate to customer success to coordinate limits and credits.
- Step 4: For multi-tenant risk, enable temporary global backpressure: redwood routing set-backpressure --level medium --reason "noisy-tenant"

D. Model quality regression (semantic failures)
- Step 1: MQL triage: collect 25 failing prompts from the evaluation pipeline; confirm regression beyond baseline.
- Step 2: Pin traffic to previous stable model variant with canary controls:
  - API: PATCH /models/v1/variants/traffic {"variant":"v1.4-stable","percent":100}
- Step 3: Block automated deployments of the suspect model and start a rollback CI job.
- Step 4: Notify product and customer success with a quality incident notice.

Staged communication templates (short, editable):
- Internal (first 5 minutes):
  "Subject: [INCIDENT] <short-summary> — open bridge #incident-<id>
  Body: Summary, region, observed impact, tentative cause, FR owner, next update in 10m."
- Customer short notice (within 30m if customers impacted):
  "We are investigating degraded performance for Redwood inference in <region>. Some requests may experience increased latency or errors. We will provide updates every 30 minutes. If you are experiencing critical impact, contact support@redwood.ai and include trace-id(s)."
- Customer follow-up (when stabilized):
  "Service restored in <region> at <time>. Root cause analysis in progress. If you saw errors, a diagnostic credit may be applied; contact your CSM. Full postmortem will be published within 72 hours for major incidents."

Post-incident evidence checklist (must be collected before any runbook reversal where possible):
1) Export time-series for affected SLOs covering T-60m to T+120m (retain raw metric granularity).
2) Capture top 200 traces and store as artifact linked in the incident bridge.
3) Snapshot serving pool topology (node list, versions, kernel/driver versions).
4) Export deployment/change events (CI/CD run IDs, manifest diffs).
5) Collect any tenant telemetry and sample user payloads (redact PII) used for debugging.
6) Record exact CLI/API commands executed and times.

On-call rotations and runbook ownership:
- Rotation template (compact):
  - Primary (1 week): SRE primary handles pages, 1-hour response SLA.
  - Secondary (1 week): covers for primary during business hours, response SLA 4 hours for non-P1s.
  - Shadow (30 days): new hire shadowing rotation to build competency.
- Ownership: runbooks should have a named owner and be reviewed quarterly. Use the label runbook-owner:<team> in metadata for tracking.

Game day plan (30–90 minute focused exercise):
- Objective: validate decision ladder, execute a KV eviction scenario, and practice customer comms.
- Participants: FR, BO, 2 SREs, 1 MQL, 1 CSL.
- Script steps: 1) Inject synthetic latency into pool A, 2) Observe SLO alert, 3) Execute Latency runbook A, 4) Practice customer short notice and update cadence, 5) Debrief.
- Scoring: time-to-stabilize, correctness of decision ladder steps, quality of comms.

Postmortem and learning cadence:
- For P1s: full postmortem with timeline, impact table, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and owners within 72 hours.
- For P2s: condensed postmortem within 7 days.
- Action closure: owners must provide evidence of mitigation in PR or runbook update.

Runbook hygiene and governance:
- Owners update runbooks after every incident that used the playbook.
- Quarterly tabletop to validate runbook steps and sample commands.
- Keep playbook compact: prefer <25 steps and explicit CLI/API commands where possible.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Check regional p95 (example):
  curl -sS "https://monitoring.internal/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{region=\"eu-west-1\"}[5m])) by (le))"
- Scale pool example: redwood infra pool scale --region eu-west-1 --pool inference-pool-42 --delta +4
- Rollback deploy example: redwood deploy rollback --service kv-cache --to tag/2026-05-21
